articles.title: Mermaid Guide - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: One of the most exciting pieces of Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea Expansion is that you can leave behind your human form (temporarily!) to become
articles.body:
One of the most exciting pieces of Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea Expansion is that you can leave behind your human form (temporarily!) to become a mermaid. Yes, that means you get a customizable mermaid tail.

Becoming a mermaid or merfolk is one of the first things you will do in Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea Expansion. Aside from owning the expansion, the only requirement to start the expansion content is to have unlocked Ursula and have her live in Dreamlight Valley.

First, head over to your mailbox at home. A note is in there from Ursula. Read the letter, and the storyline will begin. Ursula will tell you to meet her by a cove right by the Cursed Cave. Meet her there. She'll hand over a Strange Gem which will allow you to turn into a mermaid or merfolk . Customization options are immediately available, with different tops and tails, hairstyles, jewelry, and eyes, among others. (More customization options unlock as you play.)

To become a merfolk, approach a body of water and press and hold the button indicated. (This will be different depending on the platform you're playing on.)

There's plenty to do in your mermaid form: catch fish, pop bubbles, and explore underwater. There are two ways to swim: underwater and at the surface.

Swimming at the surface is what you'll do in bodies of water on the main map in Keepsake Sea. While doing this, you can catch fish and gather materials . Use your movement buttons to move around, just was you would with walking. Catching fish requires you to sea comb . Push the indicated button, which on PC is LB , and hold it to dive. When you swim through ripples, you will catch fish. You will also automatically pick up materials and fish while swimming outside of ripples, too. This consumes energy like other activities do.

When you approach Mermaid Statues with whirlpools and push the indicated button, you will enter Keepsake Sea's underwater world. Besides just being beautiful, there's plenty to do down here, too. You'll move by using your joystick, mouse, or directional buttons, but swimming up and down uses didn't ones. On PC, these are the left and right triggers.

You can pop bubbles underwater both just for fun and to collect Star Coins and materials floating inside. Pushing the indicated button to Surge forward pops them, but also consumes energy. You can return to dry land by swimming back through the whirlpool .

You will also be able to find and open Green Chests scattered about the area. They're often hidden at the bottom of the ocean.

There are resources to be collected here, too, like Dark Pearls, Mermaid's Purse , and Electric Eel Kelp .

You can customize your eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw, hairstyle, body, face paint, facial hair, ears, tail pattern, fin, and hands. There are a lot of options unlocked from the start, but more become available as you find or unlock them in-game. You will also be able to change the surge effect that flutters behind you as you swim quickly in the depths.

We're updating this guide to include a full list of customization options.

articles.title: The Enchanted Ship Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: After meeting Captain Jack Sparrow in Captain of the Dead, the previous Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion, the Captain informed
articles.body:
After meeting Captain Jack Sparrow in Captain of the Dead , the previous Quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley's Keepsake Sea expansion , the Captain informed you that he could fix up the Legendary Adventurer's ship so that you can sail to find the next Guardian! In the Quest The Enchanted Ship, help the good Captain repair the ship so you can go sailing!

Head through the Infernal Fortress to find yourself in a new area, Galleon Gulf. Jack Sparrow will be on the dock on the left side of the area. Talk to him there. He tells you that, long ago, the Legendary Adventurer had a magical ship, but it was destroyed on the rocks long ago.

Captain Jack Sparrow believes that he can restore the ship if you find the five missing Enchanted Ship Parts around Shipwreck Shores. They can be found in the following locations:

The Enchanted Crow's Nest can be found in Barnacle Bay. It is located to the right of your House, behind a small wooden fence. Because it is not assembled, it looks like a sparkling pile of planks.

The Enchanted Wheel is in Peddler's Post. It is on the left side of the area, between two wooden buildings and behind a fence with skeletons painted on it.

To find the Enchanted Sail, you'll need to head to the Infernal Fortress area. At the very southern edge of the Infernal Fortress, there is a small body of water. The sail is the water, inside some golden ripples. You can either fish it out or use your merfolk form to pick it up by swimming through the ripples!

On the far right side of Galleon Gulf, opposite the dock where Captain Jack Sparrow waits, is a secret hidden beach. Head to the very right edge of the area, where there are large trees in and around the water, and turn into your merfolk form. Swim straight ahead until you reach the beach - the Enchanted Crane is on the left side.

On the right side of the secret beach, opposite the Enchanted Crane, is a green chest containing a blue clothing bag with the Pretty in Pearl merfolk torso item inside!

To find the Enchanted Anchor, you'll need to change into your merfolk form and use any Whirlpool in Shipwreck Shores to enter the Doubloon Depths.

The Enchanted Anchor is at the far southern end of the Doubloon Depths, where you first swam with Dory during the Quest The Four Guardians . To reach it from the main whirlpool at the Barnacle Bay dock, swim straight until you reach a floating platform, then turn left, then turn right when you see a large ship's wheel decoration on the ocean floor.

Once you have all five items, bring them to Captain Jack Sparrow, who will still be on the dock of Galleon Gulf. Jack Sparrow says that it will still be a while until he can finish fixing your ship - but, it turns out you will be plenty busy, as Milo Thatch appears and tells you he has deciphered the last part of the treasure map!

The final Keepsake you need to find is beneath Sharkfin Isle. Jack Sparrow tells you that the drawbridge to Sharkfin Isle is broken, but gives you the Drawbridge Lever Handle to repair it.

To reach the Drawbridge, head back through the Infernal Fortress and turn right. Head straight to the wooden steps at the edge of the area and climb them.

At the top of the stairs, there is a sparkling pole to your right. Interact with it to place the Handle, then interact with the Handle to lower the Drawbridge. Walk across to find yourself on Sharkfin Isle!

Sharkfin Isle is shaped like a shark. Walk along it until you reach the tail, where you will find a hidden beach with a Mermaid Statue in the water. Turn into your merfolk form and interact with the whirlpool to dive into the fathoms below!

Once again, you will find yourself in an underwater area that is separated from the rest of Shipwreck Shores' undersea by a magical smoke barrier. A Helmet floats in the water in front of you - interact with it to make the first Sunken Echo Puzzle appear!

Read the note in front of the puzzle. The Legendary Adventurer was mocked for wearing their enchanted helmet. You need to remove their tormentors and surround them with their loyal crew instead!

Complete the puzzle by following the steps below:

Interact with the bench on the right side of the puzzle to push it out of the way. Now, a glowing path appears that allows you to move people around.

There is a pointing person to the right of the Legendary Adventurer. Interact with them and they will move out of the way.

Now, find the cheering person just past the bench you moved. Interact with them and they will move to stand next to the Legendary Adventurer, replacing the pointing person.

Interact with the trash can on the left side of the puzzle. It also moves out of the way, and another glowing path appears.

Push the pointing person to the left of the Legendary Adventurer. They will move out of the way.

There is another cheering person in the back corner of the puzzle, past the trash can. Interact with them and they will stand to the left of their friend, replacing the pointing person.

One more pointing person stands on a rotating platform in the center of the puzzle. Interact with them to turn them around so they are facing away from the Legendary Adventurer.

Once you have completed all of the above steps, the puzzle will be solved and will disappear!

Once again, read the note at the front of the puzzle. This time, there's a bit of a logic puzzle to solve! The Legendary Adventurer and their crew want ice cream, and you need to match each crew member to their favorite kind of ice cream.

The Legendary Adventurer is wearing their Helmet and likes banana ice cream.

The First Mate is wearing a pirate hat and likes chocolate ice cream.

The Navigator is wearing a sailor's cap and likes chocolate ice cream.

The Lookout is wearing a bandana and likes banana ice cream.

Complete the following steps to match each crew member to the correct ice cream flavor:

There is a rotating platform in the center of the puzzle. Turn it two times until it is pointing towards the chocolate ice cream.

Interact with the First Mate in the pirate hat, who is on the right side of the puzzle, to push them towards chocolate.

Turn the platform one time. Now, it points toward banana ice cream.

Interact with the Legendary Adventurer, on the left side wearing a helmet, to match them with banana ice cream.

Turn the rotating platform three times to return it to the chocolate side.

Interact with the navigator in the sailor's cap, on the left side of the puzzle, to assign them to chocolate ice cream.

Rotate the platform one time to point it at banana ice cream once more.

Interact with the last remaining child - the lookout in the bandana - to give them their banana ice cream.

With the children all content with their ice cream, the puzzle disappears!

Read the note. The Legendary Adventurer and their friends are enjoying their ice cream, but you need to clean up the area!

You can clean things up by completing the following tasks:

Pick up the three piles of trash. One is to the left of the table, one is on top of the table, and one is to the right of the table, hiding behind the first mate in the pirate hat.

Pick up the umbrella hiding inside the bush. Put it on top of the table where the Legendary Adventurer and their friends are sitting.

Pick up the boot full of flowers, on the ground to the left of the table. Put it on top of the table where the Legendary Adventurer and their friends are sitting.

Now, the area is clean, and the solved puzzle disappears!

As you've solved all of the Sunken Echo Puzzles, the Bottled Helmet appears in front of you. Pick it up and the barrier disappears - this area is now no longer cut off from the rest of the Doubloon Depths!

Return to the Galleon Gulf dock and talk to Jack Sparrow. Your ship is ready - now you've got your very own pirate ship to sail!

You can summon your ship by interacting with the bells that appear at the ends of docks throughout the Keepsake Sea. There is a bell right at the end of Galleon Gulf's dock, so give it a try!

When you interact with your ship, you are given three options: Captain's Cabin, Customize, or Sail. Captain's Cabin takes you to a private space with access to a Crafting Station, Cooking Station, and Storage Chest. You can also decorate this space as you like!

Customize lets you decorate your flag and sail as well as choose up to four Villagers to crew your ship. You can assign one Villager each to the Bow, Crow's Nest, Left, and Right locations.

Assign Captain Jack Sparrow to the Bow position. For the other three crew members, you can choose whoever you like! (You are also able to sail your ship without a crew if you do not want to.)

Once you've picked out a crew, interact with your ship and select Sail. Keeping the Galleon Gulf dock directly behind you, sail straight across the ocean a short distance until you see a dock in front of you. Approach it and select Dock - you have reached the Grotto of Resilience, where the next Guardian lies!

Approach the Guardian and place the Bottled Rain Boots, Bottled First Aid Kit, and Bottled Helmet on the plinth in front of her. The Guardian awakens from her slumber at last!

Talk to the Guardian of Resilience. Like her sister the Guardian of Discovery, she's not quite sure you are the Legendary Adventurer, and decides to set you a series of riddles to solve before she will grant you access to Candy Cove. However, there's something else you have to do first!

Talk to Captain Jack Sparrow. He tells you that he is tired of living in the Infernal Fortress with the Floating Skulls, and he wants a House of his own.

Return to Shipwreck Shores. You can either sail there using your Ship or teleport back to Galleon Gulf by interacting with the bell on the Grotto of Resilience's dock.

Once back, use Furniture Mode to place Captain Jack Sparrow's Hideout anywhere in Shipwreck Shores. Interact with the Scrooge McDuck sign in front of the foundation and spend 5,000 Star Coins to build the House!

This fully unlocks Captain Jack Sparrow as a Villager, so take a photo with him to celebrate. Finally, conclude the Quest by talking to Captain Jack Sparrow. He promises to help you from now on, but reminds you that you made a promise too - to help him get his ship back!

articles.title: GTA 6: Lançamento bate recorde histórico com R$ 22,5 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Game é o maior lançamento do entretenimento de todos os tempos, segundo Take-Two. Lançado nesta quinta (19), jogo vendeu 32,5 milhões de unidades.
articles.summary: Com 32,5 milhões de unidades vendidas, o GTA 6 supera marcas históricas e se consolida como o maior sucesso da Rockstar Games e da indústria global de entretenimento.
articles.body:
"Grand Theft Auto 6" arrecadou cerca de R$ 22,5 bilhões (US$ 3,79 bilhões) em vendas em seu primeiro dia de lançamento nesta quinta-feira (19), anunciou a Take-Two Interactive nesta sexta (20).

Com preços que vão de R$ 450 a R$ 550 no Brasil, "GTA 6" se consolidou como o maior lançamento de um produto de entretenimento da história , segundo a dona da Rockstar Games, desenvolvedora do jogo.

As empresas também confirmaram que o game vendeu 32,5 milhões de unidades antes de quinta — número que já o coloca entre os 30 jogos mais vendidos de todos os tempos .

"É com imensa gratidão que entramos em um novo capítulos da Rockstar Games com o lançamento de 'Grand Theft Auto 6'", afirmou o presidente e fundador da desenvolvedora, Sam Houser, em comunicado.

"Estamos profundamente honrados com a resposta dos jogadores ao redor do mundo e não poderíamos estar mais empolgados para compartilhar este momento com vocês."

Os US$ 3,79 bilhões conseguidos por "GTA 6" até seu lançamento superam em quase US$ 1 bilhão a arrecadação total (ao longo de meses em cartaz e de relançamentos nos cinemas) de "Vingadores: Ultimato" (2019), filme no topo das maiores bilheterias cinematográficas de todos os tempos

articles.title: Justice Warriors: The Hit Political Satire Returns With Bottom Dollar
articles.summary: AHOY Comics' hit political satire series Justice Warriors is returning in 2027 with a very topical sequel called Justice Warriors Vol. 3: Bottom Dollar.
articles.body:
If you prefer your comics with a heavy dose of political and social satire, it's hard to go wrong with AHOY Comics' Justice Warriors graphic novels. That series (which is now being developed as an animated show by Chapo Trap House ) is back for a third volume titled Justice Warriors: Bottom Dollar, and creators Matt Bors and Ben Clarkson are both along for the ride.

IGN can exclusively reveal the cover art and first details for Justice Warriors Vol. 3: Bottom Dollar. Check out the art below:

The new volume is co-written by Bors, the founder of The Nib and a multiple-time finalist for the Pulitzer Prize, and Clarkson, a filmmaker and veteran of Adult Swim. The book is also illustrated by Clarkson. Here's the official summary for Bottom Dollar:

The cataclysmic, violent, and deeply satirical Mega-World Games are coming to futuristic Bubble City, and Officers Swamp and Schitt are on deck to help clear out the Uninhabited Zone slums to make way for the landing of a stadium ship. The number one sport is Joust Punch, the extremely cool and extremely deadly sport wherein motorcycle riders hit each other with their fists. But when the Prince’s sports bets bankrupt the city and he furloughs the police, Schitt and Swamp join up for Joust Punch in order to win both the game and the “game within the game" of side-betting in order to get themselves out of debt. The stakes get higher, more complicated, and more corrupting as every character is pulled in, and the gambling spectacle that undergirds the games threatens to swallow the entire economy. There's a lot riding on the final match…

“JUSTICE WARRIORS: BOTTOM DOLLAR is a dystopian sports story for a world where no one can get ahead and everyone, from the fans to the ref, have an app in their pocket capable of ruining their lives with a single bet,” said Bors in a statement. “Incomes are strained and household debt has reached a record high of $19 trillion. Half of men are now using gambling apps where the only winners are U.S. Army Special Forces placing Polymarket bets on the governments they will violently overthrow the following morning. Sports are no longer a contest of athletes, but a financialized spectacle for addictive gambling apps. BOTTOM DOLLAR is about how debt and desperation has turned everything, from our entertainment to our own homes, into a casino where everyone is pitted against each other and the house always wins.”

Justice Warriors #1: Read the First Issue for Free

Justice Warriors Vol. 3: Bottom Dollar is priced at $19.99 and will be released on May 12, 2027. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop or preorder a copy on Amazon .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Yaga Episode 6 Review: In Its Most Disturbing Episode Yet, New Reveals Have Us Shocked to Our Core
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Yaga Season 1, Episode 6. Episodes 1-6 are now streaming on AMC+ in the US and Crave in Canada, with new episodes releasing on Fridays at midnight PT.

Trigger warning: This review has references to sexual assault and non-consensual behavior depicted in the series.

Yaga Episode 6 dives into its deepest depths thus far, giving us answers that were left unknown from last week’s episode while revealing horrifying experiences in the town of Whittock.

Following Geena’s daughter, Lily, showing up at Katherine’s door throwing up blood, we see the aftermath of her being treated in the hospital, along with Carson and Rapp catching up on everything that’s occurred up to this point.

As Billy meets with Carson and Rapp at the hospital, we’re given a handful of details as to what happened with Lily, including that she experienced some type of trauma, they found both hallucinogens and chicken blood in her body, she threw up a tooth, and that she was 8 weeks pregnant – but not anymore.

With Lily being only 14 years old, this is alarming and horrific for multiple reasons. As Geena eventually allows Carson into Lily’s hospital room, the truth is finally revealed: Henry raped Lily. As she explains the details of that night, we see a flashback of Henry in a floral crown holding a chicken at one of his parties that he invited Lily to, where she also believed she was drugged as she couldn’t tell real from fake during portions of the night.

During the act, she remembered seeing Logan standing in the corner, listening. Afterwards and before she passed out in the bed, Henry said she was just drunk and she was misremembering what had happened. She starts to question if it was actually her fault, and instantly Carson and Geena tell her it was absolutely not.

After Lily shared her frightening experience, Geena went to report it to the police – however, Eckert wouldn’t submit the report. He ended up going to her home and trying to bribe her with $50,000 to keep quiet about it all.

Even after bringing Lily to the hospital the next day to get a sexual assault forensic exam, Geena all of a sudden saw Eckert show up, who forced them to leave and go back to their house. He went as far as physically assaulting her and breaking her wrist, threatening that if they tell anyone about the sexual assault, the next person will be hurt even worse. “He’s on the [Parks’] payroll,” Geena told Carson, “I thought you were too. Sometimes I think the whole fucking town is on the payroll.”

Right as we think the details of Lily’s trauma are finished, she informs both Carson and her mom for the first time how she found out she was pregnant (one week prior) and the steps she went through to terminate the pregnancy the night before. Due to being afraid of getting an abortion at the hospital because of the Parks’ power in the town, Lily went with a suggestion from Pam – to go to Laney and complete a ritual at a cabin in the woods.

We see flashbacks of people in the witch masks in the same clearing of the woods that Rapp previously found, with chickens and bones around as Lily describes what she had to do. This included swallowing Henry’s tooth, which had fallen out of his mouth after Pam had previously punched him, and killing and drinking the blood of a chicken as people chanted around her. After being left alone eventually, she felt very sick and walked back to town – making it only as far as Katherine’s house. When asked by Carson why Lily hadn’t told her mom about the pregnancy, Lily deflected, saying she was tired.

It’s apparent that Carson thinks Geena killed Logan and did something to Henry, as she recounts her own sexual assault from high school, and says how her mom wanted to kill the guy who did it to her. She tries to create a safe space for Geena to admit it, as she finally says, “Ya know, I wish I had killed both of them,” and continues stating she was happy when she heard Logan was dead – and she hopes wherever Henry is, that he’s dead, too.

At this point, we see Rapp has found out Geena returned a rental car the same day he checked his out and saw the box with the podcast recording in it – he assumes she left it in his car for him to find, so he breaks into her house to see if he can find anything suspicious. As he’s later on the phone with Carson, who’s filling him in on the revelations and reminding him they have to listen to more of Logan’s tapes to hear the sexual assault, Rapp hears Geena come home. The sound of her opening the door startles him and he knocks a carton of eggs from the counter onto the ground – they immediately break and spread all over the floor.

As Geena walks into the kitchen and sees the broken eggs, she instantly goes to her closet to grab a shotgun, right as Rapp is running out of the house as quickly as he can. He bolts into the backyard and hides behind her chicken coop, where she sees him go and fires a warning shot at the coop. She slowly walks around to find him holding up a shovel in defense, and then we see the sudden shock on her face as she lowers her gun and is staring at something on the ground behind Rapp.

Rapp, confused, turns around to see what she’s looking at – and we see Henry’s corpse lying in the chicken coop. The camera slowly pans up his naked, bruised body, and we see – just like Logan – Henry has also been castrated.

Somber music follows as we see Eckert take Geena away in handcuffs, along with Henry’s body being transported to the morgue.

The episode winds down with Carson inviting Rapp to her place – which is a cozy houseboat – and he shares more about his past and present working for the Parks, including how his dad did the dirty work for the family, cleaning horrible situations like this up for them.

As he’s processing his grief and feelings, Rapp admits he thinks he knew Henry was this type of person – despite always seeing him as a little brother and not wanting to believe it – due to allegations and situations that occurred in the past where the Parks paid people off to make things disappear. “But never with a minor,” he says, still looking shocked.

Carson alludes to Eckert making a move on her the night before (when Rapp was with Katherine and ignoring her texts) as she herself is processing how he could do something as awful as to try and cover up Lily’s sexual assault. During their conversation, Rapp also makes clear that he knows Geena didn’t kill Henry. He said the shocked look on her face was a major tell that she had no idea he was lying there dead in her backyard. The last two episodes will hopefully reveal the truth regarding whether Geena did kill him or who is framing her.

The vibe starts changing as the two of them begin to sit closer together and start flirting sweetly with one another, with Rapp saying how he “wants to kick the shit out of Eckert” the next time he sees him, even though he knows Carson handled things on her own.

They start kissing and getting intimate – even though Rapp flirts with everyone and just slept with Katherine literally the night before, there’s an underlying sweetness to the two of them together in this scene. An honesty that seems to come across when he’s with Carson specifically, and he tells her, “You’re so fucking beautiful” right before they have sex. It feels like he genuinely might mean it.

The narrator closes out the episode while we see more shots of Carson and Rapp together, as she says, “A witch with a child would never die, and wouldn’t that be fucking scary?”

Episode 6 has a theme of witches without children, with multiple narrations referencing it throughout, and the various references to pregnancy make you wonder if Carson will potentially end up getting pregnant after what happens in this scene… or if they’re going in an entirely different direction for the last two episodes.

As we wrap up this latest episode, perfectly titled, “Mother Witch,” it seems more obvious that Baba Yaga and the “witches” in the masks are more likely strong women from the town who are trying to protect one another from the horrors around them – by any means necessary. This would explain the suspicions of Katherine, Yelena, and even Pam, as they tend to hold back knowledge while also forming relationships with Henry and Logan.

The final two episodes of Yaga will be airing together on November 27.

articles.title: Christian Bale Explains Why He Created His Husky Batman Voice at the Last Minute During Auditions
articles.summary: Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.
articles.body:
Christian Bale has revealed why he improvised his iconic gravelly Batman voice at the last minute during his Batman Begins audition with Christopher Nolan.

Rather than the throat-shredding performance being something Bale had practiced beforehand, the American Psycho and Big Short star has admitted that he simply took a gamble on the voice while in the moment — and after beginning to feel self-conscious about how his natural tone sounded emanating from the Batsuit.

"Being in that suit, I just felt like it was really stupid just to talk normally," Bale explained while appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , adding that he had been given Val Kilmer's ill-fitting cast-off for purposes of the audition. Kilmer, of course, starred as Batman in the 1995 entry Batman Forver — meaning the costume was a decade old by the time Bale pulled it on.

The 10 Greatest Batman Costumes of All Time

"And so on the day I went 'ah, they're going to hate it but I'm going to go for it.' And I started doing this more bestial guttural voice. I went back home and showed my wife what I'd done and she said 'well, you've blown that one, haven't you?'"

On the contrary, however, Bale said he later discovered that "Chris Nolan... loved it," and the rest is history. Bale went on to be cast as Batman for the director's acclaimed Dark Knight trilogy. Nolan even added another husky mouthbreather for its third entry, as fellow British actor Tom Hardy left audiences looking for the subtitles during his scenes as Bane.

"I'm running around, a grown man dressed as a bat in rubber," Bale recalled of his audition. "I can't just talk like I'm hanging out. There's got be something deeper and darker and more monstrous to make this work."

In the years since, Bale's take on Batman's voice has become "iconic" — and that's according to Robert Pattinson, the current Bat, who told GQ that it had been "almost impossible" for him not to do similar when picking up the cowl, even though he had found it difficult to maintain during extended dialogue scenes. "It's so kind of iconic, the voice he was doing in it," Pattinson said. "[And] it's really, really hard."

Pattinson is next set to appear as the Dark Knight in the upcoming The Batman: Part 2, which will now launch in February 2028. While not confirmed, Pattinson's new commitment to James Bond could end his run as the DC Comics hero, meaning someone else will have to cough up their own take on Batman's voice in the not-too-distant future.

articles.title: GTA 6's No-Nonsense Cops Are Scaring Players Into Actually Following the Law
articles.summary: GTA 6's cops are meaner and easier to provoke than ever before, leading many players to obey the law and keep their head down early doors.
articles.body:
Back in the day, the thing we were most looking forward to in any new Grand Theft Auto game was going on a big killing spree for absolutely no reason. I'm sure many of you were waiting to do this in GTA 6 , making the most of all the new details Rockstar added to the long-awaited sequel.

However, now that GTA 6 is finally in our hands, there's a curious phenomenon throughout the player base: no one really wants to commit any crimes. Instead, it seems most of us are spending the early hours of the game going about our day-to-day lives while keeping our heads down. Some of us are even using turn signals when we're driving.

So, why are we playing GTA 6 so differently from the games that came before it? A likely theory is that crime just isn't worth the risk like it once was — the cops really mean business this time.

"2 hours in GTA 6 and I haven’t committed a single crime outside of missions," said X / Twitter user @BearsShowYo . "That new system got me spooked lmao," added @JuJu_Da_Gamer . "The cop system in GTA 6 is crazy lmao I’m genuinely scared to steal a random car," @OvOBrezzzy commented .

MDRRR, pitié j’ai jamais vu ça #GTA6 — Pado 💭 (@Pacino_Tilley) November 19, 2026

They're far from alone in this. "Went into someone's backyard, they threatened to call the police and I genuinely feared for my life man," said @NohanDGreece. "I jumped into the water to get away asap." "Have been a good boy so far, using my own car and minding my business, those MF are brutal," @hissdigg said. "I can’t go home because I’m wanted in my own neighborhood and I don’t have any money to change clothes," added @Adeux_ailes.

Worse yet, the cops have never been easier to set off. Some will even attack you for filming them arresting someone else.

NEW: GTA 6 cops DO NOT like it when you film them stealing money and brutalizing people during stops. — Cinemarxism (@CinemarxismBret) November 19, 2026

NEW: GTA 6 cops DO NOT like it when you film them stealing money and brutalizing people during stops.

Because the cops pack so much of a punch this time around, it's completely changing how players interact with the game. "I was texting a friend a few hours into my playthrough that I was annoyed a taxi ride to my (Jason's) house was $162 because I didn't want to walk and she was like, 'Why tf can't you steal a car???'" said @BlueOwlzMedic. "It honestly didn't even occur to me."

"Out here stopping at red lights… cops got me committing no grand theft or auto," added @DallienceRNG .

The biggest change to how the cops work in GTA 6 is that they're a lot harder to shake off . It isn't just a case of outrunning them until they get bored; you've really got to put in the work to avoid getting busted.

First, you flee the scene. That gets them off your case for now, but they will still be hypervigilant in the area you committed the crime. So, you've also got to change vehicles, mix up your appearance, get a new disguise, and make sure you're not hanging out with the person you committed the crime with. Oh, and you better not be walking around while openly carrying a weapon, because that's a quick way to get them on your case as well.

Another change is that there is now a 6-star wanted level in GTA 6 . It's incredibly difficult to achieve, but if you can pull it off, you're in for a hell of a survival mode. And I really do mean survival mode, because it's impossible for the wanted level to decrease once you have six stars.

articles.title: GTA 6 Doesn't Officially Have First-Person, but You Can Force It to — Here's How to Do It
articles.summary: GTA 6 may not have launched with the option to play it entirely in first-person, but where there’s a will, there’s a way. Players have already worked out how to switch from the default third-person perspective, and it requires quite a few fiddly button presses.
articles.body:
GTA 6 may not have launched with the option to play it entirely in first-person, but where there’s a will, there’s a way. Players have already worked out how to switch from the default third-person perspective, and it requires quite a few fiddly button presses.

While you can’t play through the whole of GTA 6 from behind Jason and Lucia’s eyes, there are certain moments where that is a valid option. These include clicking in the right analog stick while holding the left trigger with a weapon unequipped to enter “inspect mode,” which lets you get a closer look at things when standing still. Another instance is when pulling up your phone while driving, which puts you behind the wheel, making steering a bit harder while checking your texts.

But now the GTA 6 community has unlocked a way to switch into genuine first-person, allowing you to roam Leonida, fire your guns, and rob stores from much closer to the action. Here’s how to do it, although we can’t guarantee how long this method will last before Rockstar issues a patch fixing it.

Note: this appears to currently be working on both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

Use the bumpers to move across to the ‘CONTROLLER’ tab.

Scroll down to ‘Touch Pad Button’ or ‘View Button’.

Press either Circle or B to put the phone away, while spamming the ‘Camera’ button. If that doesn’t work, repeat the steps: bring up your phone and smash that ‘Camera’ button until it works.

It might take a few tries, but once done, you’ll now be locked into first-person for the rest of your session. Dying won’t reset it, but reloading your save or quitting the game will.

Just like the method, the results are by no means perfect, though. It’s a little buggy, with some jank to be found with aiming a weapon, or certain animations not quite agreeing with this glitched version of first-person. It does, however, give us a glimpse of what the future may look like for GTA 6. After all, GTA 5 didn’t receive an official first-person perspective option until it was released on PS4 and Xbox One in 2014, a year after its first launch.

And, of course players are already using this forced first-person perspective to try to see Jason and Lucia naked in the shower . Under normal circumstances, can Jason and Lucia get naked in GTA 6? We've got the answer .

So, will you be putting this first-person bug to the test? And when do you think Rockstar will include it in an official patch? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: GTA 6 Display Settings Explained — Our Recommendations for Motion Blur, Brightness Reduction, and More
articles.summary: While we'll have to wait a little while longer for a PC version of GTA 6 that you can tweak to your heart's content, there are still some visual dials you can tune to get Vice City looking just a little bit better.
articles.body:
While we'll have to wait a little while longer for a PC version of GTA 6 that you can tweak to your heart's content, there are still some visual dials you can tune to get Vice City looking just a little bit better.

There is a display page in the GTA 6 settings menu that you can get to by pausing the game and going to 'Settings.' Then, hit R1 (PS5) or RB (Xbox) until you get to the 'Display' tab. There are several options available, which are mostly aesthetic, but there are some things you can adjust, like Motion Blur, that can change the way the game feels.

The first couple options are Brightness Calibration and Safe Zone. For the former, adjust the brightness bar until the Rockstar logo is barely visible. I know it's tempting to crank the brightness to make it easier to see things in the environment, but with how much emphasis GTA 6 puts on immersion, it's really just best to follow the instructions here. Plus, I haven't really had any situations where the environment was too dark to see what I'm doing — not yet, at least.

The Safe Zone setting just adjusts the borders of the screen. I'd leave this at its default setting unless there are parts of the game that are getting cropped out of the picture. Then, adjust using the D-pad untill all the white border icons are just visible on the corners of your display.

The next three settings — Player Status Effects Intensity, Hit Effects Intensity, and Awareness Effects Intensity — adjust the way that the screen effect alert you to what's going on with your character. I keep all of these maxed out because I like being able to react as quickly as possible. But if they're distracting for you, you can turn them as low as you'd like, just be warned: It'll probably make the game a little bit harder.

Then, there's motion blur. Full disclousure, I do not like motion blur at all, so I usually turn this down to 1 or 0. Basically what it does is introduce a blurring effect to your surroundings whenever you move the camera or your character quickly. Turn it up if you like it, turn it off if it gives you a headache.

The dismemberment toggle is pretty self-explanatory. Turning it on will show when limbs are taken off with certain types of injuries. Turn it off if it makes you queasy. The blood and gore intensity slider is a similar beast. By default it's set to high (3/3), but you can adjust it to either limit the amount of blood or turn it off altogether.

GTA 6 also lets you change the way that flashbangs affect your screen. You can either set it to bright, which will white-out your screen whenever you get flashbanged, or set it to dark, which will do the opposite. This is a godsend for playing at night, especially if you don't want to wake anyone up with a super bright flash on your TV.

Then there's brightness reduction. This might be the most impactful display setting for GTA 6, as it "applies a filter to the world that softens the output of bright lights without impacting the HUD." And while that might sound appealing for anyone with sensitive eyes, just be warned that it drastically changes the way the game looks. It ends up giving the world a washed out, almost blown out aesthetic that is decidedly less appealing to look at. Make sure it's turned off unless you're specifically looking to reduce the brightness of lights in the game. Luckily, the game will warn you when you toggle it on, and makes you confirm your choice before it actually goes into effect.

Finally there's high contrast shaders. This is actually an awesome accessiblity feature, and lets you assign high contrast shaders to the player, allies, enemies and interactive objects to make it easier to spot everything. GTA 6 is a visually busy game, and if you're visually impaired in any way, this can make the game a lot easier. The setting will turn on all the shaders by default, though you can toggle each of them individually. Players are yellow, allies are blue, enemies are red and interactive objects are gray. You can also change the fill opacity to make it less garish.

articles.title: GTA 6 Has Only Been Out For a Day and People Are Already Asking Take-Two's Boss About GTA 7
articles.summary: GTA 6 has finally arrived after more than a decade of waiting, but apparently that's not enough for some people. Less than 24 hours after Rockstar's long-awaited sequel launched, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7.
articles.body:
GTA 6 has finally arrived after more than a decade of waiting, but apparently that's not enough for some people. Less than 24 hours after Rockstar's long-awaited sequel launched, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7.

Appearing in an interview with TBPN yesterday, the day GTA 6 launched, Zelnick was congratulated on the game's success before being hit with a question that will haunt him for the decade.

"When do we get GTA 7?" one of the hosts asked, before quickly clarifying that he was joking.

"Once you get through several hundred hours of the most incredible fun you've ever had, ask the question again," Zelnick replied.

Fair enough. After all, GTA 6 has barely been out long enough for players to get properly acquainted with Jason and Lucia, let alone start thinking about what Rockstar might have planned for the next installment. But Zelnick wasn't quite finished being asked about GTA 7.

Later in the interview, during a discussion about AI and how technology could allow developers to create increasingly ambitious games, one of the hosts suggested that GTA 7 could theoretically be a live recreation of the entire world. Zelnick, understandably, couldn't resist pointing out the absurdity of discussing the next GTA game on the very day its predecessor launched.

"Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 November 19th. Wait, let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19th. And you're asking a question about GTA 7."

The hosts joked that they were simply moving the goalposts, but Zelnick continued to marvel at the timing.

"My father-in-law had a line about whenever he had many great business achievements and a lot of admirers. And if he ever said anything nice, he'd say, 'Oh, those are yesterday's headlines.' But it's not even yesterday. It's today."

Of course, the GTA 7 questions were firmly tongue-in-cheek, and Zelnick didn't offer any indication of when, or even if, Rockstar might release another mainline Grand Theft Auto game.

Still, given that GTA 5 launched back in 2013, and fans have spent the intervening years desperately waiting for its successor, it's perhaps inevitable that people are already wondering just how long they'll have to wait for GTA 7. For now, though, Zelnick would probably appreciate it if everyone could at least finish GTA 6 first.

articles.title: Marvel’s DNX Crossover Finale Ends in Tragedy for the X-Men
articles.summary: Marvel's X-Men/Fantastic Four crossover DNX ends in tragedy. Here's what you need to know about the final chapter and how it reshapes the X-Men's future in the Marvel Universe.
articles.body:
After months of drama, Marvel's DNX crossover has come to an end. This major X-Men/Fantastic Four crossover wraps as we knew it would, with one last showdown between Cyclops and the Chairman, the fallen Hank McCoy. And by the time the dust of this battle settles, the X-Men are faced with a major tragedy and an arguably even bigger problem ahead.

Read on for a full breakdown of what happens in the DNX finale, but beware of spoilers for DNX #5!

At its core, DNX is an ideological conflict between Cyclops and his former friend, Beast. Both mutants saw a future where mutants dominate the planet in the Age of Revelation crossover. Cyclops seeks to prevent that future, while the Chairman (which has become the de facto name of this version of Beast to distinguish him from the younger, cloned version who still serves with the X-Men) wants to bring it to pass by any means necessary.

In recent issues, the Chairman nearly succeeded in detonating a bomb to transform the residents of Juniper, PA, into mutants, but the bomb was only partly successful. The mutants in question were deformed and barely clinging to life. The Chairman now hopes to destroy the town and try again elsewhere, while Cyclops seeks to save these poor, tortured souls and stop his old friend for good.

The two mutants battle it out amid the ruins of Juniper, with the Chairman lashing out because he feels that the X-Men abandoned him when they should have helped him save mutantkind from extinction. Cyclops manages to stab out one of the Chairman's eyes and incapacitate him, and he then sets about disarming the villain's bomb. But the Chairman attacks him again before Cyclops can finish deactivating the bomb's batteries.

As the fight continues, Cyclops finally seems to break through to his old friend and make Beast understand he's been wrong. But it's too late for either of them. Ultimately, the bomb detonates with one battery left attached, which creates an explosion just large enough to vaporize both Cyclops and the Chairman. Juniper has been saved, but at the cost of the life of the X-Men's intrepid leader.

The X-Men have little time to mourn the death of their leader and the corrupted version of Beast before it becomes clear that they have another problem on their hands. Cyclops shares a psionic bond with Jean Grey, who's been busy out in space in the couple of years since the end of the Krakoan Age . Jean immediately feels her husband's death, and to say she's upset about this development would be a major understatement.

Jean seems finally ready to return home, and she's not at all happy. Every other time the Phoenix has made a beeline for Earth, there's been major trouble. Wll this time be any different? Will Jean become overwhelmed in her vulnerable state and lose control of her immense power?

Based on solicitations for future issues of writer Jed MacKay's X-Men series, it looks like Jean will stay planetside and replace Cyclops as the team leader going forward. She'll also be starring in a new Jean Grey solo series, and we know Marvel has a brand-new X-Men comic ready to go called Maximum X-Men . In short, the X-Men are going to keep very busy even as they mourn Cyclops.

As is tradition these days, DNX #5 ends with a "post-credits scene" that offers one last tease for the future. It turns out that Cyclops and the Chairman aren't dead after all. Both mutants emerge in a secret laboratory, where Beast tells Cyclops, "You've slept long enough. I am only now realizing that we both have."

It seems that Beast managed to teleport them both to safety as the bomb detonated. But for some reason, he's keeping their location and the very fact that they still live hidden. Even Jean's psionic link to Cyclops has been severed. Also interesting is the fact that Cyclops' uncontrollable optic blasts seem to be suppressed or contained.

Whatever mission Beast has in mind, he seems to think that he and Cyclops need to finally work together. Has this fallen X-Man regained his moral compass at long last? What is he up to, exactly? We'll have to keep reading MacKay's X-Men series to find out.

articles.title: 99 Incredible Little Details in Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.summary: From gameplay quirks to secrets and Easter eggs, here are 99 incredible little details in Grand Theft Auto 6. Don’t worry, you’ll find no story spoilers here.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here, and we’re finally getting to see what Rockstar has been cooking up for the last decade-and-change. It may be a studio already famous for its unbridled attention to detail, but just how many more tiny flourishes, references, and opportunities for emergent hilarity has Rockstar stuffed into GTA 6? The answer is a lot, so let’s get straight to it: here are 99 incredible little details in Grand Theft Auto 6. And don’t worry, you’ll find no story spoilers here.

1. From the get-go, it appears Rockstar has left no box unchecked. That is, during the Prologue, there’s a strong chance you’ll be successfully captured by the VCPD before you can effect a getaway. However, if you do manage to escape, you’ll get an extra segment of gameplay after the prison counselor addresses your initial evasion, in which she may even name-check the vehicle you used.

2. GTA 6’s selection of radio stations and podcasts is fabulous, and massively stocked with songs. Want to hear them when you’re outside of a car? You can purchase earbuds at an electronics store so that you can tune in via your phone.

3. Blood stains remain in the world for multiple days, so you may well receive a reminder of some poor behaviour on your part, even after sleeping and returning to the same spot in the days that follow.

4. Gang hideouts will reveal themselves all over the map as you progress, but one of the first you’ll probably find is an illegal animal smuggling operation tucked away in Jason’s hometown. Make sure you listen to the parrot for a clue to find more loot.

5. Speaking of animals, keep in mind that dogs will protect their owners, so consider that before you insult anyone out walking their best friend.

6. It’s also common to come across animals fighting amongst themselves, but if you spook them, they’ll typically scarper.

7. And no, it doesn’t appear that crocodiles take much interest in unconscious people that you may dump near them. But when they wake up, all bets are off.

8. The highly impressive blood tech will realistically coat surfaces the claret touches, such as covering a croc’s snout after snacking on an unfortunate fellow’s head.

9. Don’t park your car too close to the basketball hoop outside Jason’s first house. Even a well-placed shot could smash the windows of your ride.

10. Of course, cars can suffer considerably more than a busted windscreen, and car damage in GTA 6 is ludicrously good. Panels buckle dramatically, parts fall off, and dents appear exactly where they should.

11. Lose a wheel and the unfortunate rotor scraping against the asphalt will glow bright red as it dramatically heats up.

12. There’s a distinct difference in paint quality between hasty Pay ’n’ Spray jobs and professional recoats at a dedicated auto shop. Pay ’n’ Sprays offer extremely limited colours, and the paint finish has a noticeable “orange peel” effect.

13. Car glass isn’t perfect and, in the right light, you can see lots of scuffs, scratches, and imperfections.

14. Wipers will even leave visible streaks on the glass during rain, even though that’s something you’d only ever see rarely in the first-person view.

15. Businesses have their own vehicles, and you’ll spot vans and trucks across the map with all kinds of corporate and small business logos plastered on them. We’re still seeing ones we haven’t noticed, even after 120 hours, and it greatly increases the feeling of vehicle variety on the road.

16. The details on cars even extend to the fact that they have animated drivetrains – you can more easily spot when you flip a car, so take this as an excuse to get a little chaotic.

17. Some cars even have under-door lighting – an incredibly subtle effect you may well only occasionally see at night.

18. Brakes glow as a result of heavy use.

19. Superchargers make a very distinct noise, and your engine will sound different once you install them.

20. Vehicles have functioning indicators and windows, and you may even spot NPCs rolling up their windows if you’re annoying them. To use your own blinkers, tap left and right on the D-pad.

21. Truck nuts on vehicles. That’s it. No, they don’t shrink in the cold, but I’m not holding that against it.

22. Alongside the massive number of regular vehicles to discover, there are many unique vehicles sporting huge, custom decorations to find. One is a bright pink fan for a seafood restaurant that has “Our Shrimp so Pimp” painted on it.

23. There are also much, much cooler examples, including a very, very familiar Fast and Furious-adjacent green sports car with a custom paint job, tucked away in the largest house on Vespucci Island. The plate is the perfect touch, too: HAD YOU.

24. Like the cars, boats have also been lavished with attention to detail, and are typically christened with their own individual names, just like in real life.

25. And on that note, boats can now be physically launched from boat trailers, retrieved from the water again, and towed to anywhere else on the map. Same goes for jet skis and kayaks.

26. Cars and motorcycles can also be manually loaded onto trailers and towed anywhere you want. It doesn’t get around the tracker system, so it isn’t a method to cheat the new security features, but it’s still fun to fool around with.

27. Not only are jumbo jets way, way more authentically scaled – seriously, they’re huge now – but you need to enter them physically and walk to the cockpit to fly them.

28. Hijacking an enormous commercial airliner isn’t a thing the authorities will ignore or quickly forget. Soon after takeoff, you’ll be flanked by a pair of fighter jets who’ll order you to land, and shoot you down if you don’t. Jumbos are tougher than ever and will survive direct strikes from smaller aircraft, like choppers, but maybe it’s best to follow their orders.

29. Seriously, if you can see it, there’s a pretty good chance you can use it or drive it. This includes mundane work equipment like scissor lifts…

31. Forklifts (which, unlike in GTA 5, are now strong enough to lift cars)...

32. And mobility scooters. They’re not quick (obviously), but if you’d thought, surely we can’t drive those ; think again.

33. We haven’t found a go-kart at this point, but here’s hoping something eventually unlocks at the as-yet unopened go-kart track, Hot Skidz, located next to the Frontier mini golf course near Belville.

34. The out-of-order arcade cabinets you’ll spot around the world all seem to have different notes and warning signs indicating they’re busted; it’s not just a single repeated texture.

35. Not all arcade cabinets are out-of-order, though; be sure to check out GTA 6’s cheeky take on Buck Hunter in Jason’s local bar.

36. Early in the game, the band performing at The Rusty Anchor plays unique covers of songs that don’t feature on GTA 6’s radio stations, including songs direct from the original GTA: Vice City. We won’t spoil which ones, but listen up when you encounter them.

37. The cane burning taking place at one of the map’s farms is a great visual, and just one of dozens and dozens of authentic little environmental surprises and flourishes going on around the map.

38. Have you found the Christmas house in Key Lento? Once you do, make sure you find the Christmas dog, who is dressed up in green and red and ready for pets.

39. The Vice City sign welcoming tourists to the city is right where it needs to be for planes to come right over it. Michael Bay, eat your heart out.

40. You can enter Vice City’s massive airport terminal in free-roam, but you definitely shouldn’t move through airport security armed with the kind of hardware Jason and Lucia are always carrying. It probably won’t work out great for you.

41. The attention to detail extends all the way down to blink-and-you’ll-miss-them props. For instance, did GTA 6 need to have multiple power drill brands? Probably not, but it does – including a Dewalt knock-off Device, complete with yellow and black detailing.

42. Many props feature the tiniest of text you can only read if you focus on it. A can of lubricant does feel like a slight missed opportunity for more jokes, but, hey, it does at least improve penetration.

43. Rest assured there are subtle jokes galore all over the map for those willing to explore – certainly more than we can list here. These range from massive billboards with ridiculous images on, to small stealth gags on sticky note-sized pieces of paper.

44. Be sure to check your phone for all sorts of useful information. The weather app will give you the forecast for the next day, for example.

45. Surfing social media can ping new contacts and pin activities to your map well before you’d drive past them naturally.

46. Likewise, checking out physical notice boards can do exactly the same thing.

47. Skimming through magazines can also ping new discoveries.

48. There are animations for all manner of circumstances, depending on a whole bunch of factors. For instance, if you start to jog while carrying a six-pack of beer, the characters will quickly tuck it up under their armpit and carry it like a football to protect it.

49. If both your character’s hands are full, there’s a different animation for opening a chip packet with your teeth, as opposed to using two hands.

50. Similarly, there’s a distinct animation for opening cans of drink with one hand if necessary.

51. There are also different animations for opening doors when your hands are full, as the characters will use their shoulders rather than grabbing the doorknob.

52. On the topic of doors, if you park up against an object or your spot is too cramped, there’s also a different animation where your character will only open car doors partially, and subsequently shuffle out of the gap sideways.

53. And on the topic of knobs, there are.. a lot of male members in full flight in GTA 6, but, to be fair, nudity is very much a two-way street here with people of all shapes, sizes, and genders letting it all hang out.

54. You can open car doors for your partner, and it makes them fall extra in love with you, boosting your relationship stat.

55. Jason and Lucia each have a side of the bed they’ll always lie on, wherever they’re staying.

56. Getting physically close to your partner as you fall deeper in love can trigger a silent heartbeat effect in your controller.

57. We haven’t even talked about the hair yet, which is basically witchcraft. The way it moves and slides across their shoulders, or whips in the wind, or floats and sways in the water. It’s ridiculously good.

58. This isn’t the only insanely pretty technical achievement GTA 6 makes, however, and it’s honestly tough to choose what graphical astonishment is the most remarkable. Water is an absolutely massive highlight, which was an utter necessity for the geography of Vice City and its surroundings. This goes all the way from the immediately showstopping quantity of the swell and waves…

59. …to the smaller stuff you’ll notice as you really begin to pay attention. Maybe that’s the concentric rings being whipped up by helicopter downwash.

60. Or maybe it’s the countless overlapping ripples caused in the water by rain.

61. Maybe it’s the expanding splashwave you get after tossing a bloke into the water.

62. Or maybe it’s the subtle wake he generates sheepishly swimming back to shore.

63. Maybe it’s the fact that the splash seems to get bigger the higher you toss people in from.

64. Maybe it’s the uncanny quality of the refraction.

65. Or maybe it’s the fact that fish cast shadows properly underwater, even while the surface is still reflecting everything above and refracting everything below!

66. Maybe it’s a different fluid entirely, like the way drinks disappear gradually as characters sip them.

67. Heck, the attention to detail extends further than just what liquids look like – it’s sound, too. Yes, there are completely different sound effects for putting down a full can of drink compared to an empty one.

68. Or is it the ludicrously pretty lighting – particularly how insanely good dawn and dusk look?

69. It’s a tough question because, seriously, it only really gets better when the sun goes down. Check out the wildly realistic shadows, all occurring authentically in real-time in the midst of everything else GTA 6 is doing.

70. Check out the glow of light in water. It looks ridiculously good.

71. We haven’t even mentioned the effectiveness of reflecting light off surfaces like the bright sheen on road signs from harsh headlights, or the highly realistic strips of cat’s eyes lining the roads.

72. And, look, if we want to talk about reflections, the TV is mirrored in the glass frames behind the couch.

73. The shiny chrome work on a truck will also reflect surrounding details. It simply doesn’t stop; everywhere you look, something eye-catching is happening, or there’s something to hear.

74. RydeMe drivers hate it when you don’t close the door for them.

75. And if you ever cross a driver, you’ll be temporarily banned from using the app for fast travel.

76. Hop into a chopper after sprinting and you’ll hear your character still catching their breath as they put on their headset.

77. The World War 2 novel in Jason’s first house leans heavily into the classic hometown nickname trope for its soldiers, only they’re all in-universe GTA cities, like Liberty, Gellhorn, Alderney, and Carcer.

78. Thrown knives will get embedded in walls and doors, and can even open doors from the force of the impact.

79. You can manually raise and lower bridges over the various waterways and create insane jumps.

80. Pool balls collect dots of chalk dust on them.

81. Clothes only get wet up to the point you were in the water.

82. Punching bags are crushed temporarily where you strike them.

83. You can leap out of moving buses when commuting on them.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

84. There are multiple references to the prolific “before GTA 6” meme, including a social post decrying the fact that the Barnyard Blue video game arrived before Race ’n’ Chase 7, and a Righteous Slaughter T-shirt making a similar gag. Righteous Slaughter on the JoySystem when?

85. Speaking of the JoySystem, the indie walking simulator Tenebrae Lux is credited to a fictional creator called Johannes Zuch, who’s Bogarted the whole production and whose name appears relentlessly on screen throughout. In other words, it walks like a walking simulator, but it quacks like a Hideo Kojima parody.

86. Speaking of Bogart, I don’t know how many GTA 6 players are going to be familiar with the 1948 Humphrey Bogart noir film Key Largo, but I appreciate GTA’s take: The Key Lento, which can be found in a collection of thrift shop DVDs on the island.

87. Unlike GTA 5, GTA 6 has a host of different fast food chains you can enter. You can even use the drive-thrus.

88. The physics handling the dragging objects behind your cars is genuinely brilliant. In fact, there’s so much Fast & Furious in this game I’m very surprised I haven’t stumbled across an ejecto seato yet, cuz. That was the one set in Miami, after all.

89. Some clocks are animated and show the right in-game time at any given moment.

90. Characters will automatically rest sunglasses on top of their heads when they get home, and drop them back over their eyes when they leave.

91. You can find a mini Arthur Morgan riding an equally tiny dog at Frontier Mini Golf.

92. You can also find Arthur’s cowboy hat at a Port Gellhorn yard sale.

93. If that’s not your style, you can always opt for a McClane Ventilation Specialists hat from the Hamlet thrift store. Die-hard fans of McClane’s ventilation expertise will even be able to find his actual warehouse a few streets across town.

94. In a room near the top of a tower, near Donnie’s trailer, is an old analogue TV that displays the logo for GTA: Vice City’s Malibu Club. Or, at least, it does once you flip a switch and hit a button.

95. The pre-order bonus ’55 Vapid Stanier car is available from the Ocean View Hotel from Chapter 3 onward. In GTA Vice City, you’d often see similar Oceanics sitting in front of that game’s version of the Ocean View.

96. In The Rusty Anchor bar, you’ll find a vintage poster of Love Fist’s 1986 Dogs on Heat Tour, the year of GTA: Vice City, though Love Fist also overtly exists in GTA’s current HD universe. There’s a Fatal Incursion poster below, another in-universe band from GTA 5, albeit one we actually don’t know much about.

97. GTA: Vice City’s Phil Cassidy is reborn in GTA 6 as the proprietor of Phil’s Ammu-Nation, and star of the greatest commercial on GTA 6’s TV channels. No ifs, no buts.

98. Speaking of butts, however, good luck convincing anyone we need new consoles when we’re getting fully-modelled goose pimples on butt skin these days. We’re in the endgame now, ladies and gentlemen.

99. And finally, yes, if you climb to the top of the tall tower you can find just outside of Hamlet, you will find an easter egg up there. That’s the end of the sentence.

What discoveries have you made so far? What are the tiny details impressing you? Let us know in the comments. We’ll no doubt be back for another 99 in the future.

articles.body:
The Scrap Metal Queen Stoneback Crab appears in the Charting the Unknown DLC quest, Unidentified Attack . Traveling to the Dustwind Plateau to investigate the creature that attacked Yann reveals this massive machine. Our boss guide shows how to beat the Scrap Metal Queen Stoneback Crab, alongside helpful tips too.

How to Beat the Scrap Metal Queen Stoneback Crab

If you recall from other Stoneback Crab bosses, you'll need to get onto its back to defeat it. The trick with this boss type is that its vulnerabilities are always protected on its back. Regardless of how the Scrap Metal Stoneback Crab fights, it's still the same case here. You'll need to get onto its back, destroy the metal plates hiding its vulnerabilities, and then pierce them.

With all that said, you may need to dodge to the side to avoid the boss's powerful red laser. Or move frequently to not have its missile barrage instantly kill you. If you want an easy way to get onto the crab's back, use the Explosive Leap skill. This will let you leap onto its back and then use a skill like Devastation to open every vulnerability simultaneously.

After doing so, you can cling onto its back and use the Pierce button to stab each red orb. Then, you can use the same button prompt to Pull your blade out. Do this for each of the three vulnerable red orbs to defeat the Scrap Metal Queen Stoneback Crab.

Defeating the boss leads to the large metal crab shutting down as someone crawls out of the top of it. This reveals that there may be a little more to the fight than we thought! Get ready for the next boss that sort of functions as a second phase: Iron Tyrant Harkan .

articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero gives you plenty of weapons to choose from, and many are valid choices depending on what kind of playstyle you like most. While many are strong, some weapons are simply better than others. These are the best weapons in Phantom Blade Zero.

We’ve sorted our choices into three categories: best early, mid, and late game weapons. You can obtain these two early-game weapons during the game’s first two chapters, both inside the Weeping Creek Valley.

Jagged Steel is a reward for defeating Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute , in a boss fight near the Red Thread Barrier Bell in the Weeping Creek Valley. He’s the very first story boss you face in the Against the Flow main quest.

It’s a strong early-game one-handed weapon that inflicts Bleed on enemies as you land hits. When Bleed fully accumulates, Blood Loss is triggered, dealing big damage. At Lv. 5, you can start stacking Blood Blade when enemies are staggered, increasing your damage and Bleed buildup rate.

Jagged Steel is so strong early on because every enemy bleeds when hit. It destroys large chunks of HP bars with Blood Loss, which is especially useful against the first few bosses.

The Scarlet Wraithblade is a reward for beating Hua, Deadly Betrothed , in a boss fight north of the Valley Sha-Chi Tower 1st Floor Bell . She’s an optional boss that provides a real challenge early on, but her weapon is worth the effort.

The Scarlet Wraithblade is a two-handed weapon that has high shield-breaking power and a unique ability. This blade allows you to leave red spider lilies on the ground with Sha-Chi combos.

The flowers reduce enemy movement speed, sap their Sha-Chi , and explode after three seconds. At weapon Lv. 5, you can even detonate the flowers manually to gain more control over the ability.

The constant Sha-Chi depletion leads to more guard breaks , which means quick executions on normal enemies and more frequent staggers on bosses.

These two main weapons can be found in the game’s second and fourth chapters, and they can carry you through several tough combat scenarios and boss encounters.

The Outlaw Warblade is a reward for defeating Jing Ye, the Outlaw , in a boss fight near the Outlaw Trap Bell . He’s a story boss, so you can’t miss this weapon.

This is a two-handed weapon, and its unique ability allows you to siphon health from any opponents who bleed. The Sha-Chi combos consume your own HP, but the standard attacks recover your HP.

You need to strike a balance between healing and hurting yourself, but the Outlaw Warblade is an amazing weapon once you get the hang of it.

Its Power Surge has an invincible startup and locks enemies into a blood drain where you recover a large amount of HP. The relatively free healing is its greatest strength, along with solid shield-breaking power.

The Fiend Saws are a secret weapon that can only be obtained by defeating Mu Xioakui, Mistress of the Order , after collecting all of her ribbons in the Village of Lu. Gathering her ribbons before the encounter adds a third phase to the fight, providing extra rewards.

This dual-wield weapon can build up a status called Fiend-Aura Erosion whenever you hit enemies. With enough hits, the erosion erupts and erodes the target’s HP. At Lv. 5, 10, and 15, the erosion changes colors, depleting more Sha-Chi and dealing more damage.

This status effect works on any enemy type, unlike Bleed, making it versatile. The Power Surge makes all your attacks unblockable for 10 seconds , which is enough time to execute many mid-game enemies and even interrupt bosses.

articles.body:
Where Can You Use the Scarecrow Song: All Scarecrow Spots

You can use the Scarecrow Song where you see straw swirling in the wind -- a big different from the original game where you had to rely on Navi to point out a secret, but invisible, spot. You can use our interactive map to find all the spots where Adult Link can utilize Pierre to create an additional Hookshot target (just search for Scarecrow Spot).

Play the Scarecrow Song to summon Pierre at the start of the labyrinth with the Moblins to get on top of the stone walls and bypass all challenges. This also allows for quick access to the Fairy Fountain and Gossip Stones.

Walkthrough Page: Forest Temple Mysteries

Location: Northeast outdoor courtyard, above the side door on 1F

You get here after dropping through the twisted blue hallway. Pierre leads to Gold Skulltula #52.

Return to Dodongo Cavern as Adult Link and you can find a Scarecrow Spot that wasn't accessible when you first completed the dungeon. Look for it on the first floor in the eastern potion of the dungeon. Enter the main lava-filled hall and jump over the pillars to the right walkway, then head south and through the open doorway. The Scarecrow is up to the left in the long hallway that follows. You'll be able to get a well-hidden Gold Skulltula by hookshotting up to it.

Walkthrough Page: Disaster in Goron City

Lava platform east of the Fire Temple entrance. From the low platform, look for the higher one with the straw gust.

Broken bridge at the end of that path, up to the right. The high ledge has a ring of Rupees around a Purple Rupee.

3F, above the rolling-boulder room. Push out the stone block, hop north, then look back south and up. This leads to a Gold Skulltula.

There are three Scarecrow Spots in the Lake Hylia area.

1. Scarecrow Spot - Lake Hylia Fishing Pond

Stand below the docks on the north side of the dried-up lake. Summon Pierre and hookshot up to the Fishing Hole entrance. The Scarecrow Song guide calls this your first one to try.

Walkthrough Page: Disaster in Zora Domain – Ice Cavern

Location: Southwest islet, near the large tree

Head to the southwest island on Lake Hylia via the connected bridges. From the southwest corner of the large tree, look toward a small islet with some shrubs on top. While you can swim across later when the water level is high, you can get here with Pierre's help even earlier and get a Red Rupee.

Walkthrough Page: Disaster in Zora Domain

3. Scarecrow Spot - Lake Hylia Laboratory

Location: Lake Hylia Lakeside Laboratory, northwest side

Go to the Hyrule Laboratory and stand on the hill on the northwestern side of the building. You can barely make out the swirling straw up top on the roof. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon Pierre and then use the Longshot to get up on top of the roof. This is an alternative to getting a Piece of Heart that would otherwise require you to plant a Magic Bean as Young Link.

Walkthrough Page: All Heart Piece Locations

Pagoda tower room, the 3F ledge by the water-level mural. This is a shortcut back to the mural. The walkthrough mentions it twice: once when you drop down to the pagoda, and again later “from the southwest corner.” Both look like the same spot.

Skeletal ship dock, high ledge to the west above the shortcut lift. Pierre leads to Gold Skulltula #85.

Above the western wall of the pit where the ship sank. Get there from the fallen bird statue. The ledge has pots, and one holds a Fairy.

Statue room, high ledge above the west hand. You need the Longshot. Pierre leads to the temple’s last Gold Skulltula (#99).

On the first and main floor at the center of the Proving Grounds. You can find the Scarecrow Spot on the second floor in the round room with the columns and the eye rock at its center. It'll enable to you to get up to the top level walkway and get a crucial Small Key 8.

articles.title: Macaulay Culkin to Return as Kevin McCallister in Home Alone Sequel
articles.summary: Macaulay Culkin has reportedly signed on to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel for Disney.
articles.body:
Macaulay Culkin has reportedly signed on to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel for Disney.

Details on the original child actor's return to the franchise were originally reported by Puck . The project, which would see Culkin slip back into the mind of one of the most mischievous characters in movie history, is said to be in early development at Disney – and it's already got other interesting names attached, too.

Included in the lineup of talent in the mix are The Studio and This Is the End collaborators Evan Goldberg and Seth Rogen. The comedy duo have signed on via their Point Grey banner to produce the Home Alone follow-up and will also help Culkin hammer out the details of the movie's plot.

There have been a number of Home Alone sequels since Culkin helped launch the classic Christmas franchise in the '90s, but most would agree that it's been hard to top the story of the McCallister family. Only the original film and its Lost in New York sequel managed to capture the kind of holiday magic that has brought viewers back in droves through the decades, and that's largely thanks to Culkin's performance.

The now-grown actor has remained the literal poster child for Home Alone for all this time, and in 2026, he's not just ready to come back as Kevin; he apparently pitched the idea himself. Deadline corroborated Puck's reporting and explained the extent of Culkin's involvement in its own piece. The star is said to have pitched his idea for a Home Alone return to Disney Motion Pictures boss David Greenbaum over the summer. One early idea Culkin had involved bringing Kevin back on the big screen as an older, wiser version of the character who also happens to be a dad now.

Whether Kevin would be forgetting his own children at home or dealing with burglars himself yet again remains to be seen, and it's unclear if anything from Culkin's early pitch will make it into the final picture. It's been 34 years since the star last ( officially ) played the abandoned McCallister boy, so should the early-in-development movie eventually come to be, it will bring an end to decades of fans asking for him to return.

Culkin's return as Kevin would mark his third time playing the character and the seventh entry in the franchise. The last, a Disney+ exclusive called Home Sweet Home Alone , premiered in 2021 and starred Archie Yates, Ellie Kemper, and Rob Delaney. IGN gave it a 6/10 review , saying that it "contains wit and heart, if not also clumsy messaging and some tonal misfiring."

articles.title: Satoru Gojo's English Voice Actor Didn't Realize These Wild Lines He Recorded Were for GTA 6
articles.summary: Kaiji Tang, the English voice actor behind iconic anime characters like Jujutsu Kaisen’s Satoru Gojo and Demon Slayer’s Sanemi Shinazugawa, was left stunned after learning that he had unknowingly recorded lines for GTA 6.
articles.body:
Kaiji Tang, the English voice actor behind iconic anime characters like Jujutsu Kaisen’s Satoru Gojo and Demon Slayer’s Sanemi Shinazugawa, was left stunned after learning that he had unknowingly recorded lines for GTA 6.

It seems like some of GTA 6 ’s cast are just now learning that they were featured in the game, as evidenced by a few posts circling online a day after its official global release. One of these cast members is prominent voice actor Kaiji Tang, known for providing the English voice for several main characters in popular series like The Apothecary Diaries , Kengan Ashura, and Baki , just to name a few.

In the early morning hours of November 19, Tang posted on X/Twitter confirming he was in Rockstar’s highly anticipated crime-sim. However, he revealed that he wasn’t aware the lines he recorded were going to be used in this particular game, leading to a hilarious interaction with a fan.

“I had no idea what I recorded was for this game,” he wrote. “Imagine my shock.”

“Considering they had you saying, ‘Sit on daddy’s lap,’ I’m curious what you thought it was for,” a fan replied.

i had no idea what i recorded was for this game imagine my shock lol — Kaiji Von Tang (@KaijiTang) November 19, 2026

i had no idea what i recorded was for this game imagine my shock lol

@actualcannibal i dunno demon slayer? — Kaiji Von Tang (@KaijiTang) November 20, 2026

Tang is a major figure in the voice acting business with an extensive portfolio under his belt, so it’s no surprise to learn that he lent his talents to GTA 6. Aleks Le, another popular voice actor in anime and video games, revealed that he also contributed to the project, and even said that he asked the directors for permission to include one of his famous lines from Street Fighter 6 — though it’s still unclear if that particular phrase made it into the final product.

Tang isn’t the only actor just now learning they’re in GTA 6; athlete, author, and influencer ‘Jessishiking’ revealed that they were also just now made aware of their involvement in the game.

In a celebratory post on Facebook, Jess revealed that they played the GTA series’ first-ever nonbinary character (which, to avoid spoilers, we won’t name here). They said that they were required to sign several NDAs and had no idea what they were filming for at the time due to the extreme secrecy around the game.

“Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago,” they wrote in their post. “Some fun facts: GTA was one of the most inclusive and caring sets I’ve ever been on. I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly. At the time I wasn’t allowed to know what I was shooting — I didn’t get confirmation until TODAY that it was, indeed, GTA 6.”

While the game’s full credits have since been revealed, it’s highly possible that we see more posts like this in the coming days from voice actors and performers excitedly learning that the secret project they recorded lines for many years ago is the biggest entertainment product of all time.
